We didn't want her mother there because we don't get along very well, and we wanted to avoid that stress on such an important day. However, there was an issue where I was late getting to the hospital, though not by a ton. There were still over three hours of labor left before the baby came. By the time I arrived, my wife had already called her mother and told her to come. This caused a lot of tension and made the process pretty uncomfortable for me, which in turn made it harder for me to support my wife. We didn't get the special one-on-one time with the baby that we had planned either; we had initially planned on having a full day of just us, but it ended up only being a few hours. I'm really upset about that. It's been a few weeks, and my wife asked me why I'm so moody about the topic of the birth. I exploded at her for violating the plan that we had from the beginning. First, I need to consider the dynamics of the situation. We had a clear agreement that we would be the only ones in the room during labor and birth. That was a mutual decision, so both of us were on the same page about that. However, I was late, which might have contributed to her feeling the need to call her mother for support. But I was only late by a little, and there were still several hours of labor left. So, was my lateness a significant factor in her decision to call her mother? Or was it more about her feeling unsupported or stressed? I also need to think about how I reacted when she asked me about my moodiness. I exploded at her, which led to her crying and her feeling blamed. That seems like a harsh reaction, especially considering that she was trying to understand why I was upset. On the other hand, I was upset because our plan was violated, and we didn't get the special time we had hoped for. That's a valid concern, and it's understandable that I would be upset about that. But the way I expressed my upset might have been the issue. Yelling and blaming her for something that was partly my fault (being late) could have made her feel attacked and defensive. That might have been why she shut down and refused to discuss it further. So, in this situation, am I the asshole? I think I need to consider both sides. On one hand, I was upset about the violation of our plan, which was important to me. On the other hand, my reaction to her asking about my mood was explosive and hurtful, which might have been unnecessary. I also need to think about how we can communicate better in the future to avoid such conflicts. Maybe discussing our feelings calmly and understanding each other's perspectives would help prevent similar situations. In conclusion, while I was upset about the situation, the way I expressed my feelings might have been the issue. It's important to communicate calmly and respectfully, even when we're upset, to maintain healthy relationships and avoid unnecessary conflicts.
